sections.history: Thirukkannapuram lies in the Kaveri delta of the Nagapattinam country and is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham. It belongs to Chola Nadu and was hymned by five Alvars: Thirumangai, Nammalvar, Kulasekara, Andal and Periyalvar, who describes the shrine as enduring even through the deluge. The temple is believed to have been built by the Cholas, with later additions by the Thanjavur Nayaks. The sthala purana adds that a king raised it with the help of Vishwakarma. It is counted among the Pancha Krishnaranya Kshetrams.
sections.architecture: A granite wall encloses the shrines and three of the temple's seven bodies of water, among them the Nitya Pushkarini and the Ananda Saras. The sanctum faces east, where the Lord stands as Neelamegha Perumal, the dark-blue cloud, with the Goddess Kannapura Nayaki in her own shrine. The festival image, Sowriraja Perumal, is the form carried in procession.
sections.legends: The name Sowriraja carries a story of the hair. Tradition tells of Ranga Bhattar, a poor priest, who once offered a garland a second time. The visiting king found a hair in it, and the priest answered that it was the Lord's own. The Lord is then said to have appeared with thick tresses, and sowri, hair, became part of his name. Another tradition recalls Vibhishana, who longed to see the Lord walk: on every Amavasya the Lord is brought out to give him darshan, in the Nadai Azhagu Sevai.
sections.festivals: The Brahmotsavam is the great festival, when the festival image is adorned with hair in the procession in remembrance of the sowri legend. A chariot festival is held in Vaikasi, and Masi Magam is observed in the month of Masi. On every Amavasya the Lord is brought out for Vibhishana's darshan, and pongal is offered at the last puja of the day.
sections.experience: A deeply devotional shrine, rich in the voices of five Alvars and in its local stories. Spend time at the east-facing sanctum and the tanks within the granite wall, and if you can, come on an Amavasya to see the Lord brought out. Brahmotsavam days are the most crowded; confirm festival dates locally.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; festival days are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thirukkannapuram lies in the Nagapattinam district of Tamil Nadu, in the Kaveri delta. Tiruvarur and Nagapattinam are the nearest larger towns with railheads, and Tiruchirappalli is the nearest major airport. Reach it by road, and confirm local directions on the way.
